📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has unveiled he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the tech giant. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox said Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the manufacturer's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

"I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My strategy was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

In a recent development, wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally debuted last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Sources indicate that wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a fresh studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

It has been revealed that paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The timeless series finds itself in a bit of a predicament, with Dragon Quest 12 taking forever to come out, and the tragic passing of franchise artist Akira Toriyama only adding to the surrounding uncertainty.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't think the future of Dragon Quest has ever seemed so murky.

The timeless series finds itself in a bit of a predicament, with Dragon Quest 12 taking forever to come out, and the tragic passing of franchise artist Akira Toriyama only adding to the surrounding uncertainty.

And while the recent remakes have done well to fill the gap, it does feel like fan patience is becoming stretched for the first time in ages.

Case in point: the newly revealed Dragon Quest RPG The Cursed Tree and the Chosen Isle — a mobile spin-off set to launch next year — has been met with a surprising amount of frustration.

Japanese social media has been full of disgruntled fans; some have, again, grown annoyed by the series' relative stagnation, while others have voiced their displeasure over Dragon Quest's continued use of Toriyama's unmistakable art style.

One viral post has a pop at the new mobile game's protagonist, simply pointing out that Toriyama would never have drawn a scabbard that doesn't match its sword's length.

In other words, the quality has fallen off without Toriyama — and yet Square Enix is still crediting him as the character designer.

But what's really caused a fuss is a short blog post by veteran video game composer Yasunori Mitsuda, who worked on Chrono Trigger alongside Toriyama.

In a recent development, in the post, Mitsuda offers his own thoughts on the aforementioned drama. He remains respectful, but it's clear that he's got strong feelings on the state of Dragon Quest as a whole.

"I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Akira Toriyama fans, and even for the late Akira Toriyama himself," Mitsuda explains.

He continues: "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly fresh no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end, and [series creator Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG.".

Industry observers note that "What's notable is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future. But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

In a recent development, so, what are your thoughts on Dragon Quest at this point in time? Are you feeling similar frustrations? Strike down some slimes in the comments section below.

[source procyon-studio.com, via powerupgaming.co.uk, automaton-media.com].

  • Knowing that “Roughstock” was inspired by his own experiences, I asked Mo Brings Plenty, who plays Mo in Marshals and Yellowstone, about details in the episode he was happy to see included.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for Season 2, Episode 6 of Marshals are ahead! You can stream the series with a Paramount+ subscription and catch new episodes on CBS every Sunday.

In a recent development, the episode of Marshals that just aired on the 2026 TV schedule is inspired by a tragedy that actually happened to one of its stars and American Indian Affairs Coordinator, Mo Brings Plenty, and his family. In 2024, his nephew, Cole Brings Plenty, died, and a coroner ruled out foul play. His family disagreed with that, and they’re still looking for answers. In this week's episode of Marshals, Mo’s nephew, Troy, is found dead, and he and Kayce work to prove that it was a murder, not suicide. Ultimately, the case is left unsolved, and according to Mo Brings Plenty, that was a very vital detail to include.

Knowing that “Roughstock” was inspired by his own experiences, I asked Mo Brings Plenty, who plays Mo in Marshals and Yellowstone, about details in the episode he was happy to see included. He immediately noted that he was glad the case was left unsolved, because that kind of outcome happens in real life, often, as the actor explained:.

Oh, I was happy to see that when the police officer noted he just kind of blew it off, because that's really the case. And so I was happy that we highlighted that legitimate part of it. Not every officer is that way, but in some cases, in some states - primarily states that have a high American Indian population - that occurs.

When I spoke to Mo in March this year about an episode of Marshals having to do with missing American Indians, he told me they “haven’t got any answers for” what happened to his nephew, Cole.

Sources indicate that in this episode of Marshals, it’s made very clear that while Troy’s case will stay open, it will likely go unsolved. It’s obvious that it’s not being prioritized by law enforcement, and despite the marshals best efforts, there is no solution as to who killed Troy by the end of the episode. When I asked Mo why it was notable for this episode to go without a solution to Troy’s case, he said:.

In a recent development, because the wheel of justice doesn't turn for us as American Indian people, and of course we're tax-paying people as well. And so, you know, first responders get their funding through taxpayers, tax funding, and so when it doesn't work for us, then it's so frustrating. It's like, ‘Well, why are we even paying taxes?’ And so that's one of the things that is impactful for me, and that I need to continue to speak about because it is occurring.

Recent findings suggest that in the case of Mo’s real nephew, Cole, he was found dead a few days after he was reported missing and named as a suspect in a domestic violence case. Two years later, Mo spoke to THR and claimed that his nephew’s death had gone “uninvestigated,” while the Lawrence Police Department said there was “no foul play involved in Cole’s death.”.

When I spoke to Mo about this topic recently and how it was represented on this Yellowstone show, he remarked:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It's sad for me and my family, especially when I hear the cry for other nationalities and in foreign countries, when the very same thing is occurring to us as the original inhabitants within this country, we're basically flying over mission fields to get to mission fields.

According to the U.S. Department of the Interior Indian Affairs, there are “approximately 4,200 missing and murder cases that have gone unsolved.” And when I asked Mo Brings Plenty if Marshals could ever circle back to Troy’s unsolved case, he noted:.

Industry observers note that absolutely, it could definitely happen. But you know, there are so many stories. I mean, my family is not the only family. This isn't the first time something like this has occurred in real life. You know, there are many stories, many families, different situations, different circumstances that are going through the same thing.

Sources indicate that overall, he was clear that there are lots of stories like his that should be shown on Kayce’s Yellowstone spinoff. He’s not the only one who has lost a loved one in this way and was left without answers, and he’s hoping to see more of those stories depicted on Marshals.

It has been revealed that now, to see how Mo’s story continues, you can watch the next episode of Marshals on November 22 at 8:30 p.m. ET, and you can stream it the next day on Paramount+.

After two weeks of multiplayer downtime, Dark Souls 2 & 3's mysterious server "problem" has been fixed, so it no longer feels so lonely online

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Developer FromSoftware has declared that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.
  • FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server problem".
  • FromSoftware never specified the exact concern impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has declared that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server problem". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

FromSoftware never specified the exact concern impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently revealed - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

Tech Report: Splatoon 3 version 12.0.0 upgrade debuts November 17

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gematsu

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nintendo will release the version 12.0.0 enhancement for Splatoon 3 on November 17, the company declared.
  • According to recent reports, sections marked “on Nintendo Switch 2″ apply only to Nintendo Switch 2.
  • Made it possible to participate with a friend in traditional X Battles as a group of two.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nintendo will release the version 12.0.0 enhancement for Splatoon 3 on November 17, the company declared.

According to recent reports, sections marked “on Nintendo Switch 2″ apply only to Nintendo Switch 2. All other changes apply to both Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.

Changes to Anarchy Battle (Series).

Made it possible to participate with a friend in traditional X Battles as a group of two.

Changes to GameChat on Nintendo Switch 2.

Added a feature that allows players to open GameChat and invite friends from their group while playing modes with friends, such as battles or Salmon Run.

This patch focuses on making changes to matchmaking and multiplayer balance.

According to recent reports, for X Battles, we have added a feature to allow players to play as a pair with a friend. The goal of this feature is to expand the range of ways to play, and we will introduce it on a trial basis starting in Chill Season 2026. After we have introduced it, we will comprehensively analyze how these battles are actually played and how the gameplay situation shifts, including for players who are not playing with a friend. Then we will decide whether to continue providing this feature in future seasons.

For Anarchy Battle (Series), we have changed the matchmaking system such that, in exchange for removing the feature allowing players to continue with the same team, matchmaking will now complete more rapidly and with less imbalance of skill level and equipped weapons between players and their opponents.

Industry observers note that for Challenges, we have changed how Challenge Power is calculated to make it easier to raise Challenge Power the more wins a player has. With this change, between players who would have ended up with about the same Challenge Power under the previous system, the player who attained the greater number of wins will have the higher final Challenge Power.

For multiplayer balance, we made a variety of changes to main, sub, and special weapons, including changes to the flight distance of Blaster shots.

Recent findings suggest that with most weapons, when a player fires while moving, the player’s movement speed is added to the shot’s speed to a certain extent, resulting in a more natural trajectory. For Blasters, we have minimized the change in shot flight distance caused by this effect, making it easier to maintain an appropriate distance against an opponent’s Blaster.

Among the special weapons, we have changed the Reefslider because, while there is statistically little impact on victories in matches between extremely skilled players, it has a high impact on matches between less skilled players. The intention behind this change is to alleviate that striking difference. By narrowing the area affected by the explosion we have made it so that players cannot reap the maximum benefit without using it at the precise position. On the other hand, we have extended the invulnerability period to make it harder for opponents who used terrain to survive the explosion to counterattack and easier for the player to make follow-up attacks.

It has been revealed that for the Tenta Missiles, we have decreased the vulnerability while firing and expanded the area where it is possible to lock on to opponents. As a result, it will now be easier to use, even in situations where opponents are nearby the player. By decreasing the impact interval, it becomes easier to defeat opponents who are slow to dodge, but the duration for which they must keep dodging is reduced.

We have also added a feature for Nintendo Switch 2 that will make it easier to use GameChat.

The next update will focus on changes to multiplayer balance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hot on the heels of a monumental share price drop for the firm, Intel now faces a class action lawsuit from its own shareholders.

Recent findings suggest that this is according to an alert from law firm Robbins LLP, which recently informed all investors. This suit alleges "Intel misled investors about demand for its products and the Tech giant's future growth potential.".

The class action can involve anyone who bought stock between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026, known as the "class period".

With the memory crisis in full effect, PC sales are down worldwide (estimated to be 20% down in October), but the lawsuit argues that the PC sales slowdown was "having a materially greater negative impact to Intel’s third quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Group results than defendants had disclosed to investors.".

It also argues Intel's OEM and distribution partners were left with hardware they couldn't sell to consumers due to rising prices, and that positive impacts of Intel business coming from the AI boom were off "more than offset by the negative effects on the Manufacturer’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup.".

The suit also alleges that Intel's reporting of its operations and ability to capitalise on the AI boom "were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects.".

With Robbins LLP informing investors of this class action lawsuit, it's possible more could join the claim, and we don't actually know how many are currently in the class action right now. The law firm notes that those who purchased stock in the class period have until January 12, 2027, to join.

Recent findings suggest that it's important to note that Intel stock prices have dropped significantly, declining by 29% at the end of the last month, and upwards of 40% in the last six months. From $95.53 per share on Wednesday, October 28, to $59.66 per share as of the time of writing, that's a 38% decline. To a shareholder, that is a straight devaluation of however much money they would have put into the company in that period.

Sources indicate that intel has had its fair share of ups and downs over the last few years. With a long history behind it, Intel made a killing in the '90s and '00s, becoming a market leader for CPUs, but unstable chips and underperforming chips marked a downward trend for the company. This is all while TSMC has surpassed it in chip manufacturing and AMD has managed to pull ahead in the gaming CPU market. The decline in PC sales thanks to the memory crisis only made things worse for Team Blue.

Intel doesn't appear down for the count, with it gaining market share from AMD just last week (and its recent handheld chips are excellent). Still, some of Intel's own shareholders alleging they've been misled is certainly not a great look for a organization that is still very much on its way back up.

The Witcher 3 uses gen-AI to enhance Geralt's Polish voice following actor's stroke - "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically"

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
  • In a recent development, the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.
  • It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

In a recent development, the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a company called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

"The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

Game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

Industry observers note that this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce fresh voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

According to recent reports, "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

The third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game rolled out. It adds an entirely fresh region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

Sources indicate that in preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.

It has been revealed that A big part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a fresh game plus mode.

In a recent development, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

Sources indicate that in any case, the patch goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

According to recent reports, overall, a bit of a smaller revision compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something crucial or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

'Game dev isn't always straightforward': Overwatch's director responds to players upset about season 6's hero being a DPS

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "We’ve seen a lot of discussion about the (DPS) role of the season 6 hero.
  • "When we started work on the detective, he was a support.
  • Last week we found out a few fresh things about the next hero coming to Overwatch in season 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"We’ve seen a lot of discussion about the (DPS) role of the season 6 hero. We understand that you were looking forward to another support hero next season and I hope that giving context for the decision will help players understand it, even as some of them are disappointed.".

"When we started work on the detective, he was a support. But as time went on and the kit continued development we realized that it wasn’t working. Once we tested Hudson as a DPS, the turn around in our feelings for him was instantaneous and dramatic. This decision ultimately wasn't whether we release a DPS or a support hero, it was whether we release a great character or one we didn't believe in. Building heroes for OW is as much of an art form as a technical challenge." via a social media post.

Last week we found out a few fresh things about the next hero coming to Overwatch in season 6. He's an omnic detective, his name's Hudson, he has a fun accent, and he will be a DPS. Hudson is the last hero to be released from the batch teased earlier this year during Overwatch's Spotlight, and after all this time I'm very excited to see what he has to offer. But not everyone shares this sentiment.

Industry observers note that there's a good chunk of players who are upset about Hudson, before they've even tried him out, simply because he's not a support hero, which was what Team 4 initially promised him to be. I've seen this discontent online and honestly ignored it, thinking it was either bots or people farming for attention because I cannot fathom why anyone is honestly upset about this.

Industry observers note that I've been maining support in Overwatch for almost 10 years now, ever since open queue grinded me down and I accepted that no matter how much I liked DPS, I had to role fill if we wanted to win games. So, after all these years I love getting my hands on a fresh support hero, but after four new supports this year (including Sombra's transition to the role), I'm more than satisfied with the role's current diversity of heroes.

It has been revealed that but Team 4 is taking the criticism seriously, as Keller has addressed it directly. Aside from trying to convince players that shoehorning a hero into a role just because that was the proposal 10 months ago isn't a great idea, he also explains how "game dev isn't always straightforward" and how the team needs "to adapt to create the best version of something".

I completely agree. I'd much rather have a hero that was crafted for a role holistically than one forced into it to fill a quota. Letting the people who know Overwatch the best, aka the devs, have the freedom to craft heroes and change them when needs be is what will ensure the best possible outcome.

This is such a non-problem, especially considering how strong the support roster currently is. Look at our poor tank players for example, forced to switch between Orisa and Mauga every game. Go give them some love and attention, lord knows they need the energy much more than us over in support.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
  • Recent findings suggest that after days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has revealed Huang's resignation as company president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately.
  • Sources indicate that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

Recent findings suggest that after days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has revealed Huang's resignation as company president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

Sources indicate that "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, notes she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

It has been revealed that nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the company: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a tech giant-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Recent findings suggest that nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the tech giant's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big new lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

Sources indicate that if the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

It has been revealed that there's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as big a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the latest one on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam.
  • Recent findings suggest that newly introduced turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

Earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

Recent findings suggest that newly introduced turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

According to recent reports, "We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input glitch on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

In a recent development, amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar issues, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

"Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we revealed earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer reveals a newly introduced launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

Valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

"I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

And apparently, deciding where to spend the holiday has become a little complicated. Per a new report, the newlyweds want to celebrate with both families without making either set of parents feel left out.

The Grammy winner and her Kansas City Chiefs tight end husband on married July 3 at Madison Square Garden, an event Kelce later described as one of the best nights of his life. Now, Rob Shuter alleges in his Naughty But Nice substack that the newlyweds have been discussing their first Christmas together. Per Shuter, an insider claims:.

Sources indicate that neither wants to disappoint their parents, but they also don’t want their first Christmas as a married couple to become a tug-of-war. They want everyone to feel included.

It's a familiar holiday scheduling problem, although the families involved are rather more recognizable than most. Swift's parents, Andrea and Scott, have long been central to her Christmas celebrations, while Kelce remains close to his mother, Donna, and father, Ed. Swift even grew up on a Christmas tree farm in Pennsylvania, an experience she later turned into a holiday song. With both sets of traditions to consider, choosing where to spend the holiday allegedly hasn't been straightforward.

The Kelces already have some well-established food traditions. Kylie Kelce has praised Swift's baking alongside Donna Kelce's famous dinner rolls, so there would apparently be no shortage of people willing to contribute to Christmas dinner.

Also, the couple may already have a solution in mind. Instead of traveling between family gatherings or deciding which parents to visit, Shuter's sources says Swift and Kelce are considering hosting Christmas themselves. The idea would bring their relatives to one celebration, although no final aims have been publicly announced. A second source told Shuter:.

It has been revealed that they think bringing everyone together is the perfect answer. They get to start their own traditions without making either family feel they’ve lost out. It’s about creating one major family Christmas.

Sources indicate that there's at least one reason a gathering away from a football stadium might be easier this year. As it so happens, the Chiefs don't have a game scheduled on Christmas Day in 2026, according to the team's published schedule. Kansas City is set to host the Upcoming England Patriots on Dec. 21 and the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 27, leaving Christmas Day free of a game-day obligation.

Sources indicate that last Christmas looked a little different for the couple. The Chiefs played the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Dec. 25, with Swift and her parents in attendance. She and Kelce also surprised several stadium employees with Christmas gifts.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Kelce has already talked about looking forward to his first Christmas as a married man. Earlier this month, while promoting Tommy Hilfiger's winter collection, he told Women's Wear Daily he was excited to start new traditions with Swift. Although there's at least one he's apparently keeping: his mom Donna's homemade blueberry muffins.

Recent findings suggest that the families have spent Christmas together before. Back in 2023, the “Shake it Off” performer's brother Austin showed up at a Chiefs game dressed as Santa Claus and surprised Kelce with a Christmas present. Both families also played a part in the couple's July wedding, with Austin serving as Swift's man of honor and Jason Kelce standing beside his brother as best man. The newlyweds even asked guests to make charitable donations instead of bringing wedding gifts. So, getting everyone together for Christmas wouldn't exactly be a first for the newlyweds.

Industry observers note that neither Swift nor Kelce has confirmed Shuter's report, so where they'll spend Christmas and whether both families will be there remains to be seen. Industry observers note that when you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space to be empathetic compared to previous entries.

It has been revealed that "Crime is a fundamental part of GTA - at least up until now, it has been," Nelson told The Guardian (via @GameRoll_, ta IGN) in a newly introduced interview. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out." When asked about whether this will be the first GTA game to encourage people to be empathetic, Nelson responded, "I would say so. I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to.".

I am deeply curious as to what those mechanics may be, given that most of what we've seen so far is pretty relegated to shootin', lootin' and a bit of smoochin'. If you steal a car, is there an NPC that loses their job because of it? Can you repair the harm you caused through that action? I'm sure hardly anyone else that's vibrating through their skin in excitement for almost having the game in their fingertips will be asking such questions, I'm just often wary of empathy mechanics in games.

In any case, doesn't matter all that much for us PC lot just yet, especially because Rockstar are preparing themselves both legally and technically to tackle pirated copies of the game. Rockstar will obviously be quite busy at the moment too, not just because of that whole launching a game thing, but because UK-based workers will be voting to unionise as we speak. If formed, it could be 1600 members strong, which would make it the biggest games union in the UK. Solidarity with all the workers as the voting process continues. I hope you get the result you deserve.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Publisher Spike Chunsoft and developer Gemdrops have released new information, video, and screenshots for Danganronpa 2×2 introducing details about the Class Trials featured in Slayhem Mode, including the new Akimbo Consensus system.
  • When a murder occurs among the students, an initial investigation takes place, followed by a Class Trial.
  • During a Class Trial, parties may voice various, often conflicting, testimonies, causing the discussion to become chaotic and difficult to follow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Publisher Spike Chunsoft and developer Gemdrops have released new information, video, and screenshots for Danganronpa 2×2 introducing details about the Class Trials featured in Slayhem Mode, including the new Akimbo Consensus system.

■ A Latest Class Trial System: Akimbo Consensus.

When a murder occurs among the students, an initial investigation takes place, followed by a Class Trial. This is where Slayhem mode introduces the latest Akimbo Consensus system.

During a Class Trial, parties may voice various, often conflicting, testimonies, causing the discussion to become chaotic and difficult to follow. This is the point where Akimbo Consensus comes into play. You must evaluate the validity of each statement and use either an “Affirm” or “Refute” Truth Bullet to address it, thereby organizing the discussion and steering it in the right direction.

Industry observers note that once you have correctly organized the statements, three options will appear at the end, allowing you to decide what should be discussed next. If you make the appropriate choice, it is considered a “Consensus,” and the Akimbo Consensus is successful. The Class Trial will then proceed in the direction you have established.

Slayhem Mode Also Utilizes a Familiar System From a Previous Title.

According to recent reports, slayhem mode also includes the Debate Scrum that was featured in Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony. A Debate Scrum is a team-based trial battle that happens during Class Trials when the students split into two opposing groups with conflicting opinions.

■ Class Trials in Original Mode Have Also Been Refined.

This occurs when other students challenge the deductions made by the protagonist, Hajime Hinata. You can slice through their statements using Truth Blades, an element that offers a unique gameplay experience.

Sources indicate that in Logic Dive, you’ll navigate a tube-like course representing a path of synapses in the brain, dodging obstacles and answering questions along the way. Known for its high difficulty in previous game, this version includes features designed to make the experience more accessible to players.

Danganronpa 2×2 is due out for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store on January 14, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in just over one year, we will see original Lord of the Rings stars Andy Serkis, Elijah Wood, and Ian McKellen reunite in The Hunt for Gollum. However, despite now thinking of the original cast as family, Serkis didn't always feel at home in Middle-earth.

In an interview with Radio Times, Serkis revealed that at the beginning of filming Peter Jackson's trilogy, he often felt "lonely" and like "an outsider” on set. "Everyone else had already been out in Newly introduced Zealand for months before I arrived. They’d already bonded. So there was a sense of separation between them and me," said Serkis.

The Smeagol star said he and hobbit actors Elijah Wood and Sean Astin had a bit of a tiff at one point. "It wasn’t really a falling-out," said Serkis, "Well, it was a falling-out. Because of the new way we were using motion capture to film Gollum, when we were shooting scenes together, they were treating them almost like a rehearsal. So there were harsh words. But once we understood each other, we were golden.".

Sources indicate that serkis was introduced as the cave dweller in 2001's The Fellowship of the Ring, before returning to the character in The Two Towers, The Return of the King, and in The Hobbit prequels. However, due to Serkis playing a goblin of sorts, Gollum was created via motion capture, meaning Serkis was on set wearing an optical suit. This kind of technology was pretty new at the time, which explains Wood and Astin reaction.

According to recent reports, that is all water under the bridge now, as Serkis, Wood, and Gandalf star McKellan are back together to make The Hunt for Gollum. "It’s like family," said Serkis. Wood shares the feeling, as earlier this year he told GamesRadar+, "It's sort of like getting the band back together… It feels like a family reunion. My part to play is relatively small, but I'm just excited to go back and spend some time in Latest Zealand and see old friends.".

The Hunt for Gollum takes place between The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings trilogies, before Frodo and the Fellowship start their quest to destroy the One Ring. Serkis confirmed that the movie is "over a week away from starting principal photography," adding that Aragorn actor Jamie Dornan has touched down in Latest Zealand, with fellow newcomer Kate Winslet also on the way.

Sources indicate that the Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum arrives in theaters on December 17, 2027. For more, check out our guide on how to watch all the Lord of the Rings movies in order, and keep up with upcoming movies heading your way.

  • But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • Recent findings suggest that world of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

But it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

Recent findings suggest that world of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

Industry observers note that reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. At the moment, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

According to recent reports, "We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has plans to address the issue, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

World of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

It has been revealed that the idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I get my way! That being noted, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen, a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just introduced into early access.

According to recent reports, to say that it is just straight up Dark Souls combat would be unfair, from the looks of things. For one, it looks more like it leans a tad towards Sekiro with a blades-only kind of affair, whether that be massive or small. And blades a plenty they have, ranging from your classic sword, to scythes, to halberds and all sorts. It's a much flashier looking affair too, with fancy slashing effects that seem to buff moves and a pace that seems much faster than Souls games tend to be.

In a recent development, you can take part in matches with up to eight people, which presumably extends to AI (not that kind) enemies too, in "atmospheric duels, clashes, deathmatches and more." It looks neat! And best of all, unusually for a 3D arena fighter, it has rollback netcode. For those unfamiliar, and to try and explain it simply, this is essentially a bit of tech you'll find in predominantly 2D fighting games that predicts every possible input you could make in a given moment, helping to reduce lag time and allow for tighter matches (and less rage quitting).

That's a bit harder to do in a 3D environment given that you have a lot more options at your disposal when it comes to movement, so if it works that's some impressive stuff! And we could all quite easily find out together, as a demo for Rasen is available to try out. Or, alternatively, you can just pick it up whole hog on Steam right now, as it's available in early access.

#16782. Ashes of the Singularity 2 review: Some neat ideas undermined by a rubbish campaign and obtrusive generative AI

Ashes of the Singularity 2 review: Some neat ideas undermined by a rubbish campaign and obtrusive generative AI

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1833 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ashes of the Singularity 2 has some neat ideas for army management, but a poor campaign, an underwhelming new faction, and obtrusive generative AI use undermines the enterprise.
  • PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • RTS sequel in the lineage of Supreme Commander.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ashes of the Singularity 2 has some neat ideas for army management, but a poor campaign, an underwhelming new faction, and obtrusive generative AI use undermines the enterprise.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

What is it? RTS sequel in the lineage of Supreme Commander.

Reviewed On: AMD Ryzen 5 3600, Nvidia 2080 Super, 32 GB RAM, Windows 10.

It has been revealed that ashes of the Singularity 2 can't be faulted for scale. Much like its predecessor, the RTS sequel delivers on the promise of letting players control truly colossal armies. Rolling up huge globs of units and tossing them at your enemy lines in a giant, explosion-riddled mud fight is never subtle and only occasionally clever. But for any veteran RTS player, watching miles-long lines of armies clash is inevitably going to stir the soul.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, scale is also the sum of what Ashes of the Singularity 2 offers. As a sequel, it does little to build on the strengths of the original, while largely failing to address that first game's weaknesses. The campaign is terrible, the story borderline incomprehensible, and the whole experience is overshadowed by the spectre of generative AI.

Before we get into Ashes 2's numerous problems, I do want to give Oxide Games credit for one thing: for a game of this scale, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is remarkably easy to control. In terms of base-building, Ashes of the Singularity 2 is a largely familiar RTS affair. You build your production buildings, your resource harvesters, your defensive structures, and that's more or less it.

Sources indicate that when it comes to unit recruitment, however, Ashes 2 is much more interesting. While units are still recruited individually, they're also automatically assigned into armies at the recruitment phase. You build a upcoming army by queueing up all the units you want, and then when you're done, you assign a rally point for the army on the map, and all the units will just assemble there.

Once recruited, armies can be selected with the number keys and controlled like a single unit, and they tend to move and attack pretty intuitively, although pathfinding does struggle with narrow passes or rough terrain (which, to be fair are both things that real armies struggle with). This makes it very easy to oversee multiple armies at once.

Sources indicate that in addition, when in battle, you can replenish destroyed units at the press of a button, or simply set the army to reinforce automatically. It's another convenient touch, and encourages you to support your forces by constructing new production buildings close to the frontline.

It's not the only area where Ashes 2 displays an intuitive flourish. Alongside selecting the relevant structure from the menu, you can also construct harvester buildings directly from the resource node, while upgradeable buildings will often display an upgrade button over them that you can click. In terms of UI/UX design, Ashes 2 successfully minimises rooting through menus. Everything is accessible through shortcuts, directly on the screen, or a single menu layer.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, this system does come at the cost of some finer control. Unit recruitment is bottlenecked to one unit per production building type, no matter how many buildings of that type you have. This means building an army composed of specific units (such as aerial units) takes longer, so armies tend to take a similar shape. On the subject of aerial units, they are a bit of a weak point for Ashes 2. Not only are they easily countered by AA units and emplacements, they also don't match the speed of ground units when in a mixed army, with a tendency to fly off and get themselves obliterated. Regardless, army control is by far the best thing about Ashes 2.

The sequel does introduce some other new features, such as a new faction, the United Earth Forces; unfortunately it's the least interesting faction in the game.

Sources indicate that the UEF is a deeply vanilla sci-fi army, composed of tanks, jets and human soldiers so tiny they get instantly lost once the match scales up. It's way less compelling than the many mechs of the Post-Human Coalition, or the robotic insects of the AI Substrate. Where the Substrate's dreadnought units include a giant squid that fires laser beams and a blimp that shoots swarms, the UEF gets a big tank and a knockoff Megazord. Granted, the tank functions as a mobile base. That's useful, but it isn't fun.

The UEF is also the sole focus of Ashes 2's campaign. This is disappointing, but it's also the least of the campaign's problems. It's composed of 10 missions, roughly half of which are rigid tutorials with passive AI that offers virtually no challenge whatsoever.

Industry observers note that the second half, which takes place in locations across the solar system, is better. The missions actually play with Ashes 2's scale and gradually let the AI off the leash. Indeed, the final two missions offer some pretty fierce resistance. But despite being set in locations like the Moon and on a weaponised asteroid bound for earth, they're also unambitious, meat and potatoes scenarios with no real twists or turns.

The result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026.

Industry observers note that the result is four, maybe five hours of half-decent campaigning, which just isn't good enough in 2026. It highlights how generous and meticulous Tempest Rising's campaigns were, built around thrilling, rapidly changing scenarios that sought to stretch the player's skills.

It has been revealed that it doesn't help that the story is dreadful—a three way philosophy and ethics lecture between humans, AI, and uploaded post-human personality constructs. It's a parade of characters you never actually see babbling endlessly about the vague machinations of AI threats and whether or not post-humans are still the same people they were when they were bags of flesh and juice.

Ironically, the story is also where Oxide's use of generative AI is most evident. According to Ashes 2's Steam AI disclosure, Oxide used AI to "provide post processing effects and animation to art created by human Stardock artists for some of the campaign cutscenes" while "some cutscenes use Stardock human artist-made 3D assets with AI to composite the final shot." Finally, "some in-game unit barks, notifications, and a few minor characters use pre-generated ElevenLabs stock voices".

Frankly, I'm skeptical that this represents the limit of Oxide's AI use. All the character portraits look straight up AI generated to me, and the voice lines sound similarly infected. AI or not, it's something of a moot point because, either way, they're both awful. The portraits have that horrible, plasticky AI sheen to them, while the acting is often weirdly intoned in a way that does not help the narrative's bamboozling quality.

What bugs me most about Ashes 2's AI use, though, is that the RTS genre has such a rich heritage in cinematic storytelling. Warcraft 3, StarCraft 2 and Homeworld all successfully balanced their sci-fi grandeur with intimately human tales. Command & Conquer, meanwhile, was one of the earliest PC games to directly put a human face on videogame storytelling. From Kane to Tanya to Tim Curry escaping to the one place that hasn't been corrupted by capitalism, C&C's FMVs are often the thing that players most fondly remember.

According to recent reports, I understand that Oxide Games probably doesn't have a Tim Curry budget. But it also doesn't need it. C&C's FMVs aren't remembered because they're expensive, or even especially great storytelling. They're remembered because they're fun, silly, intensely human creations. You don't need a massive budget to replicate that. If Oxide Games stuck a beret on a programmer and had them ham it up in front of the camera, the result would be infinitely preferable to Ashes 2's airy, inhuman waffle.

With the campaign a write-off, you're left with multiplayer and skirmish mode. Skirmish is arguably where Ashes of the Singularity has always been at its strongest, and playing against the AI here is certainly better than the campaign, offering a wide range of difficulty levels that lets you find your own sweet-spot. Putting together a four-way grudge match, watching the scale of the conflict slowly build-out, commanding multiple armies on multiple fronts, you get a sense of what Ashes 2 could be.

None of the maps particularly spark joy.

Yet here too, there are problems. None of the maps particularly spark joy. It's a roster of generic biomes and moonscapes that offer little in the way of personality or artistic direction. Also—and this is a broader complaint—while I appreciate that Ashes 2 is meant to be a slow-burn affair, I think it is a little too slow overall. In particular, battles are too attrition-heavy, and beneath the visual fireworks, you don't necessarily feel the punch of your units in combat. When Dreadnought units clash, it should feel like two gods have descended from the heavens. Instead, it feels more like two giant snails squabbling over a particularly large leaf.

It's a shame, because the work Oxide has done to make such an unwieldy concept so, well, wieldy is impressive. Given more care and time (and less generative AI), I think this could have been a great RTS. But with the campaign such a bust, what you're paying for here is one new faction, a skirmish mode and multiplayer, and after 10 years, I just don't think that's sufficient for a sequel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.

Industry observers note that the memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong company it is today. But it's Sharma's comments at the end of the memo that are of particular interest.

While talking about what the next 25 years could bring, Sharma lamented that "too many ideas never become games" and that "too many games fall short of what their creators imagined". "For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition," she wrote. "We must change this.".

Sources indicate that sharma continued: "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

In a recent development, there is no explicit mention of generative AI here, but the language is suggestive - "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Furthermore, Asha's memo follows last month's announcement of an Xbox Labs initiative that also sounded like it was based around generative AI, despite avoiding the phrase specifically.

Industry observers note that this isn't a surprise, of course. Microsoft as a wider manufacturer is all-in on generative AI, with Copilot, and Sharma's background at Microsoft is in AI. But it's an area she's avoided speaking too enthusiastically about since her hiring as Xbox boss earlier this year. At the time, Sharma said she has "no tolerance for bad AI", and there's been such a lot else going on in the months since - including wide-ranging restructuring resulting in the loss of thousands of Xbox jobs - that the topic of generative AI has fallen into the background. Perhaps now we're seeing the sprouting seeds of it.

We've asked Microsoft for clarification.

If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical, slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty meals back in your struggling restaurant.

First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

Sources indicate that I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.

The other line reads, "Every sound effect, musical note, design decision, and line of code is human-made. Because this game is about human relationships and delicious food – and that’s not a story we would ever trust AI to tell." Thank the lord! Right now there's no release date attached to The Snackbar at the End of the World, unsurprising given it was only announced this week. But while we all wait for a date, you could perhaps join me in throwing it a wishlist on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever watched The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, you know there’s no shortage of drama. Just look at Taylor Frankie Paul, who’s had a swingers scandal, the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody complications with her children, and chaos surrounding production. But the Hulu reality series was popular and created a lot of buzz, so I was not surprised when they revealed the spinoff, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, currently on the 2026 TV schedule. However, the fact that it feels like the majority of the women in the fresh show are not Mormon and that some aren’t even wives is a bit weird and an interesting choice, considering the title, and viewers (including myself) have taken notice.

In a recent development, to catch you up in case you haven’t seen the original series, Jen Affleck, a 20-something Mormon wife and mother, joined MomTok in Utah to fight against the typical social norms and stereotypes that are common within the religion. After appearing in Season 34 of Dancing with the Stars as a celebrity contestant alongside fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt, the mother of three with a fourth on the way decided to stay in Southern California, citing the fracturing of MomTok and the need for therapy to recover from everything that happened.

Industry observers note that seeming to instead have decided to jump right into another reality series, which again is an interesting choice, Jen has brought together a new group of friends, all of whom are mothers with their own drama and secrets, but who are not all Mormon, despite the show’s name. One has even admitted to signing on for the heightened visibility reality TV brings.

According to recent reports, it’s hard not to notice that The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County is a cast divided into two groups, with the women who are Mormons being outnumbered by the women who are not. In the season premiere, cast member Aspyn Ovard (who's got a memorable storyline about being part of a throuple) says, “We’ve all been shaped by Mormonism in one way or another,” which is a bit of a vague statement when we don’t know all the details of the backgrounds of many of these women, and even she makes it clear that she’s very closed off to the church and its teachings.

I'm not the only one who has noticed this either, as this conversation has popped up all over social media, including places like Reddit, where fans have asked why non-Mormons are "even on the show." I get it's weird to call out someone's religious preferences, but when your show is called Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I do think that leads to a certain expectation.

Industry observers note that when you’re in the business of entertainment, building a franchise off of something successful and popular makes sense. But it’s hard to escape the weirdness of not really delivering on what your show’s title promises. All of this is not to say that the women who make up the OC spinoff cast don’t have compelling lives of their own, because they do, but the religious branding doesn’t entirely fit and feels like more of a subplot than a main focus, like it is in the original series.

In a recent development, and it all makes me wonder if the title should have just been something more reflective of Jen Affleck specifically? Just spitballing here.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that for a reality show that’s supposed to be centered around Mormons, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County actually positions them to be the villains of the season. McCall DaPron, the older sister of the OG series’ Mayci Neeley, exhibits confrontational behavior. She gets into frequent clashes with other cast members, often leaving them to wonder whether it’s possible to keep this friend group together.

Industry observers note that her strong commitment to her faith and her efforts to share it with others, including best friend and co-star Jordan McClanahan (whom she successfully converted), rubs anyone not as devoted the wrong way. This is especially true when her need to influence others’ opinions and actions creates conflict.

It has been revealed that the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals over four seasons, which are streaming with a Hulu subscription, but Mayci always came across like the most supportive one of the group on that show, where McCall seems less inclined to stay neutral. It’s hard to know how much of the drama is manipulated with editing, but it’s another interesting choice on a series that already seems to be trying to break its own formula.

All of this said, if there ends up being a second season of the OC spinoff, I will still definitely be tuning in!

Between Jen being pregnant with her fourth child at the same time she decides she wants a divorce, Aspyn trying to get her ex-husband to spend time with her current throuple, and Salomé Andrea figuring out if she can reconcile with a man she began dating in ninth grade and couldn’t marry in the Mormon church before she ultimately walked away from both, it is all definitely weird, but just weird enough to make me want to see what happens next.
